basis:
The deliverer offers three operations: scan a project's folder, deliver one photo, and record its
publication. When to scan, what to deliver next, what to repeat and which failure to treat as temporary
belong to the calling flow.

Syncthing may change the folder during a scan, so a scan is not a view of one instant. Each rule applies
to what its step finds when it runs, and the next scan sees the folder as it then stands. A file that
changes while it is read is judged by the bytes that were read, once, without a retry: Syncthing replaces
a finished file by renaming a new one over it, and a delivery that later reads other bytes answers
`SOURCE_CHANGED` under A3 rule 5.

3. One call delivers one photo, named by `name`, a relative path in the form a scan reports, and
   `source_id`. The service keeps no memory of earlier scans: it judges the name and the file when the call
   runs. The named file is read once, and the bytes that were read are the bytes judged, hashed and prepared.

topics.topic: Handling a zero-byte read when pre-read metadata reports a non-empty file
questions: When pre-read metadata says the file is non-empty but the single read yields zero bytes, is order 1 re-evaluated from the bytes read, or does processing continue to the signature check under order 6?

quotes:
A scan gives each regular file of the photo folder exactly one status. The first rule that
applies decides:
| 6 | does not begin with a JPEG, PNG or WEBP signature | `rejected` | `unsupported_format` |

Syncthing may change the folder during a scan, so a scan is not a view of one instant. Each rule applies
to what its step finds when it runs, and the next scan sees the folder as it then stands. A file that
changes while it is read is judged by the bytes that were read, once, without a retry: Syncthing replaces
a finished file by renaming a new one over it, and a delivery that later reads other bytes answers
`SOURCE_CHANGED` under A3 rule 5.

`size`
is the number of bytes that were read, the bytes `source_id` is the hash of; a file rejected before its
bytes were read has the size its metadata gave when it was listed.
judgement.divergence: One implementation re-evaluates emptiness from the zero bytes read and reports reason empty; another treats the metadata-time empty check as complete and reports unsupported_format at the signature check, which the calling flow observes.
judgement.why: The texts do not say whether the empty rule is re-evaluated after pre-read metadata reported a non-empty file but the single read returned no bytes.

witness.initial: A listed regular file has metadata size 1, has no placement, and is truncated before its single read returns bytes.
events: The calling flow starts a scan.
The scanner reads metadata showing a non-empty file.
Syncthing truncates or replaces the file.
The scanner performs its one read and receives zero bytes.
outcomes: The scan reports `rejected` with reason `empty`, judging order 1 from the bytes read.
The scan reports `rejected` with reason `unsupported_format`, treating order 1 as the completed metadata check and applying order 6 to the empty byte sequence.

topics.topic: Whether scanning stops at the first byte beyond the source limit or continues to EOF
questions: After a read discovers that the file grew past the source limit, must the scan stop at the first excess byte or continue to EOF, thereby deciding the rejected observation's size?

quotes: | 4 | it grew past the source limit while being read | `rejected` | `too_large` |

A scan covers the photo folder and all its subfolders (R0-12). When a subfolder that is not ignored
cannot be listed, the whole operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`, so a partial scan is
never reported as complete. A file exactly at the source limit passes that rule.

changes while it is read is judged by the bytes that were read, once, without a retry: Syncthing replaces
a finished file by renaming a new one over it, and a delivery that later reads other bytes answers
`SOURCE_CHANGED` under A3 rule 5.

`size`
is the number of bytes that were read, the bytes `source_id` is the hash of; a file rejected before its
bytes were read has the size its metadata gave when it was listed.
judgement.divergence: One implementation stops after reading the first excess byte and reports size source_limit + 1; another continues the same read to EOF and reports the full larger size, which the calling flow observes in SourcePhotoObservation.size.
judgement.why: The texts define the too_large result and define size from bytes read but do not say when reading must stop after the limit is crossed.

witness.initial: A regular supported image is exactly at the source limit when its metadata is read.
events: The calling flow starts a scan.
The scanner begins reading the file.
Syncthing appends 100 bytes before the scanner reaches EOF.
The scanner reads the first byte beyond the source limit.
outcomes: The scanner stops immediately and returns a rejected too_large observation with size source_limit + 1.
The scanner continues the same unretried read to EOF and returns a rejected too_large observation with size source_limit + 100.
